basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 22.' and it opens 'Vers. 22. Foderunt alium puteum pro quo non contenderunt. Pro tertio puteo jam victi non'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text:
Vers. 22. Foderunt alium puteum pro quo non contenderunt. Pro tertio puteo jam victi non contenderunt, quia, postquam fides Trinitatis sanctae per mundum praedicari coepit, patientia sanctorum victi adversarii cessaverunt Unde bene puteo nomen impositum est ei, latitudo. Dilatatus est enim verus Isaac, id est Christus fide omnium credentium, et notus quidem antea tantum in Judaea Deus modo vero dicitur: In omnem terram exivit sonus eorum et in fines orbis terrae verba eorum (Psal. XVIII, 5).

Moraliter puteos fodimus, quando divinae scientiae | alta sapimus vel penetramus. Quos tamen puteos allophyli terra repleverunt: quia nobis profunda Scripturarum investigantibus saepe daemones terrenas cogitationes aggerunt, ut a nobis aquam divinae scientiae tollant.
